Home.topicsSubtitle: From backyard birds to famous rivers — or mix them all.
Home.faq1Answer: Yes. Every crossword and scanword is free to play, with no account, no sign-up and no limits on how many you solve.
Home.faq2Question: Will I see the same words again?
Home.faq2Answer: No. Your device keeps a list of the words it has already shown you and leaves them out of every new puzzle. If you clear your browser's site data, that list starts over.
Home.faq3Question: Which languages can I play in?
Home.faq3Answer: English, Russian and Armenian. Each language has its own word pool, written natively by the AI for speakers of that language — not translated from another one.
Home.faq4Question: What is the difference between a crossword and a scanword?
Home.faq4Answer: A crossword lists numbered clues next to the grid, Across and Down. A scanword prints each clue inside a grid cell with an arrow pointing to where its answer goes.
Home.faq5Answer: Yes. Every puzzle you open is saved on your device with your progress, so it keeps working without a connection. New puzzles need the internet.
Home.faq6Question: What if a clue is wrong?
Home.faq6Answer: Tap the flag in the toolbar to report it. Clues reported by several players are retired and never appear again.

hero.title: A classic crossword, <mark>made just for you</mark>
hero.subtitle: Numbered Across and Down clues, a grid that grows from the middle, and words you haven't seen before.

CrosswordPage.rule1: Every white cell holds one letter. Words run across (left to right) and down (top to bottom), crossing each other.
CrosswordPage.rule2: Each word has a number in its first cell and a matching clue in the Across or Down list.
CrosswordPage.rule3: Tap a cell or a clue to start typing. Tap the same cell again — or press Space — to switch between Across and Down.
CrosswordPage.rule4: Stuck? Check a letter, a word or the whole puzzle, or reveal a letter to get going again.
CrosswordPage.faq1Answer: Choose small (up to about 14 words), medium or large (over 20 words). The grid is cropped to the words it holds, so it always fits your screen.
CrosswordPage.faq2Question: What makes a clue easy or hard?
CrosswordPage.faq2Answer: Easy puzzles use everyday words with direct definitions. Hard ones use rarer words and clues that make you think twice.
CrosswordPage.faq3Answer: Yes: type letters, move with the arrow keys, press Enter for the next clue and Backspace to go back. On a phone, the puzzle's own keyboard appears below the grid.
CrosswordPage.faq4Question: Can I share a crossword with a friend?
CrosswordPage.faq4Answer: Yes — tap Share in the toolbar to send the link. Your friend gets exactly the same grid and clues.

hero.title: Scanwords with clues <mark>inside the grid</mark>
hero.subtitle: No lists to hunt through: every clue sits in its own cell, with an arrow to the answer.

ScanwordPage.rule1: Tinted cells hold the clues. The arrow next to a clue shows where its answer starts and which way it runs.
ScanwordPage.rule2: A clue cell can hold two clues: the upper one usually points right, the lower one down.
ScanwordPage.rule3: Tap a clue cell, or any letter cell, to choose a word. The full clue always appears in the bar above the grid.
ScanwordPage.rule4: Colorful tiles are just decoration — the letters only go in the white cells.
ScanwordPage.faq1Answer: A scanword is a crossword with its clues printed right in the grid. It began as the Scandinavian crossword and is a favorite of puzzle magazines across Russia and Armenia.
ScanwordPage.faq2Question: The clues in the cells are tiny on my phone. What can I do?
ScanwordPage.faq2Answer: Tap the cell: the full clue always shows in the bar above the grid. You can also pinch to zoom, or open the full clue list.
ScanwordPage.faq3Answer: When there is no room for the clue right before its answer, it sits above or beside the first letter instead, and the arrow bends to show the direction.
ScanwordPage.faq4Answer: They're shorter — a scanword clue has to fit inside one cell, so it's a few words at most.

Rules.title: How to play
Rules.subtitle: Everything you need to solve a crossword or a scanword here — on a phone, a tablet or a computer.

sections.title: Choosing a word
paragraphs: Tap or click any white cell. The word it belongs to lights up in yellow, and its clue appears in the bar above the grid.
Where two words cross, tap the same cell again to switch between Across and Down. In a scanword you can also tap the clue cell itself.

sections.title: Typing
paragraphs: On a computer, just type — no need to switch your keyboard layout: if your keyboard is set to English, the keys type the letters of the puzzle's language in their usual places.
On a phone or tablet, the puzzle's own keyboard appears below the grid. For Armenian it has the single letters ՈՒ and և, each filling one cell; typing ո then ւ joins them into ՈՒ automatically.
In Russian puzzles the letter Ё is written as Е, as in printed crosswords.

sections.title: Moving around
paragraphs: Arrow keys move between cells; an arrow across the current direction first turns the cursor. Enter jumps to the next clue, Shift+Enter to the previous one.
Backspace clears a letter and steps back. Home and End jump to the start and end of the word. Tab leaves the grid.

sections.title: Getting help
paragraphs: Check marks wrong letters with a red strike-through and locks the right ones. Reveal fills in a letter, a word or the whole puzzle; revealed letters carry a small purple flag.
Turn on “Check as I type” in the settings if you'd like instant feedback.

sections.title: Fresh words, every time
paragraphs: Your device remembers the words it has shown you and never asks for them again. Every new puzzle is made of words you haven't met here yet.

About.title: About Crossword AI
About.subtitle: A free puzzle generator that writes in your language and never serves the same word twice.

sections.title: Why we made it
paragraphs: Most online crosswords recycle a small word list, and most translated ones read like translations. We wanted puzzles that feel written by a local author — and that stay new no matter how many you solve.

sections.title: How the words are written
paragraphs: An AI model writes words and clues directly in each language, following a style guide by native speakers: the grammatical forms crosswords use, the spelling norm, the way clues are phrased in that language's puzzle tradition.

Every word then passes automatic checks — the right alphabet, one real word, no clue that gives the answer away — and a second AI acting as an editor. Players' reports retire anything that slips through.

sections.title: How the grids are built
paragraphs: The grid itself is built by code, not by the AI: an algorithm fits the words together so every letter belongs to a real word with a clue. That is what keeps every puzzle fair.

Privacy.title: Privacy policy
Privacy.subtitle: Short version: no account, no names, no profiling. Here is everything we keep.

sections.title: On your device
paragraphs: Your browser stores the puzzles you open, your progress, your settings and a list of the words you have already seen, so they are never repeated. This stays on your device; clearing site data removes it.

sections.title: On our server
paragraphs: We store the puzzles that are created, so a shared link opens the same grid. When you report a clue we keep the report with a one-way hash of your IP address, only so that one person cannot retire a clue alone. We also count anonymously how puzzles are played (solved, which words were revealed) to tune difficulty.

sections.title: AI provider
paragraphs: New words and clues are written by Google's Gemini models. Only the puzzle settings (language, topic, difficulty) and lists of words are sent — never anything about you.

sections.title: Analytics and error reports
paragraphs: If enabled, we use Google Analytics to count page views and Sentry to receive error reports. Neither is used to identify you.

Terms.title: Terms of use
Terms.subtitle: Crossword AI is free to use, for fun and learning.

sections.title: Using the service
paragraphs: You may play, share and print the puzzles for personal and educational use. Please don't overload the service with automated requests.

sections.title: AI-written content
paragraphs: Words and clues are written by AI and checked automatically, but mistakes can happen. If you find one, report it — that's how bad clues are removed.

sections.title: No warranty
paragraphs: The service is provided as is, without guarantees of availability or accuracy. We may change or discontinue features at any time.
